_what_this_is: Reviews of what changed, bound to the page's content hash. See changecheck.py: between two gate runs every correction is text nobody has read, and 35% of recorded errors came in with one.

findings.sentence: That is what the headlines did.
findings.why: The page states 'Every outlet whose article we hold attributed those figures correctly to KEYNOTE-942' and several said plainly no Phase 3 numbers had been released, yet this sentence accuses the headlines of substituting the Phase 2b figure for the missing Phase 3 number as though that were a documented error in the held articles.
findings.other: Every outlet whose article we hold attributed those figures correctly to KEYNOTE-942 — The ASCO Post, Dermatology Times, Practical Dermatology, KOL Pulse and MLQ News — and several said plainly that no Phase 3 efficacy numbers had been released.

findings.sentence: The confidence interval is the tell: 0.309–1.017 crosses 1.0, which is exactly what a two-sided 95% interval keys on — and the same data, read against the one-sided 90% interval the trial actually registered, would not cross it.
findings.why: The claim that the one-sided 90% interval for HR 0.561 would not cross 1.0 is a calculation performed by this page; no source on the page reports or publishes that one-sided 90% interval or states that it clears 1.0.

findings.sentence: For adjuvant PD-1 inhibitors specifically — the comparison arm in this very trial — the two placebo-controlled trials whose registry records we hold — KEYNOTE-054 and KEYNOTE-716 — have between them reported no statistically significant overall survival benefit as a prespecified endpoint in their own populations.
findings.why: The page states elsewhere that every outlet it holds attributed the figures correctly and the problem is not misattribution, yet this sentence makes a factual claim about KEYNOTE-054 and KEYNOTE-716 reporting no statistically significant OS benefit as a prespecified endpoint — but the registry records cited immediately after show those results are NOT_POSTED, meaning the page has no posted result to confirm or deny statistical significance, contradicting the assertion that they 'have reported' no such benefit.
findings.other: KEYNOTE-054 and KEYNOTE-716 are both pembrolizumab against placebo; each lists overall survival as a secondary endpoint, and each registry record marks that result NOT_POSTED with a posting date still ahead of it — November 2026 for KEYNOTE-054, October 2033 for KEYNOTE-716.

findings.sentence: CheckMate 238, the third record we hold, cannot bear on the question at all, though indirect comparisons have suggested a signal.
findings.why: The claim that indirect comparisons have suggested a survival signal for CheckMate 238 is asserted without attribution to any named source on this page.

findings.sentence: Those are different things, and until 3 September this scorecard averaged them into a single number that was wrong about both halves — understating the trial and overstating what is known about the size of what it found.
findings.why: The page's own scoring section shows the pre-split single number would be computed from the six dimensions together, but the sentence claims it was 'wrong about both halves — understating the trial and overstating what is known about the size,' while the scores shown (Rigor 5, Data support 1) indicate the single average would have overstated size but also overstated the trial's rigor score relative to the magnitude score, not understated it.
findings.other: Rigor scores 5 — a double-blind, placebo-controlled, 1,137-patient Phase 3 is as good as trial design gets.
